method: scripts/ib-research/claim-check.js: the passage is copied verbatim from the live source text at the pinned revision; VERIFIED = every claim number in one sentence that shares >= 50% of the claim's content words

records.claim: The Sun's mean distance from Earth is about 1.496×10^8 kilometres, or about 8 light-minutes.
records.reason: a sentence has the terms but not every claim number (1.496, 10, 8), is not 5-80 words of prose, or shares under 50% of the claim's content words

records.claim: The Sun's mass is around 330,000 times that of Earth, about 99.86% of the total mass of the Solar System.
records.passage: The Sun's mass is around 330,000 times that of Earth, making up about 99.86% of the total mass of the Solar System.

records.claim: The speed of gravity, the speed of gravitational waves, equals the speed of light.
records.passage: Does Gravity Travel at the Speed of Light? in The Physics FAQ (also here).

records.claim: The Sun's diameter is about 1,391,400 km, around 109 times that of Earth.
records.passage: It is the largest and most massive object in the Solar System; its diameter is about 1,391,400 km (864,600 mi), around 109 times that of Earth.

narration.text: The Sun vanishes, and nobody notices.
For about 8 minutes, sunlight is still on its way.
Gravity's pull also changes only at light speed.
So Earth keeps orbiting an empty point for those same minutes.
The Sun holds 99.86% of the Solar System's mass.
Without it, Earth flies off in a straight line.
The sky goes dark, and the planet starts cooling.
So the first change arrives exactly as late as sunlight.
